source.name: UTIAS Multi-Robot Cooperative Localization and Mapping Dataset
source.citation: Leung K Y K, Halpern Y, Barfoot T D, Liu H H T. The UTIAS Multi-Robot Cooperative Localization and Mapping Dataset. The International Journal of Robotics Research, 30(8):969-974, July 2011. DOI: 10.1177/0278364911398404.
source.raw_license_status: The official page does not state a standardized open-source license. Raw archives are kept outside the public code repository and are not redistributed.

question: Under a fixed map-only localization contract and a matched likelihood-evaluation budget, how do a bootstrap PF, resample-move PF, and two QGPF-inspired transfer variants behave on two held-out real MR.CLAM robot sequences?
estimand: For each fixed dataset/robot sequence, paired seed-level difference in primary radial position RMSE between each method and B-stable; seeds quantify algorithmic Monte Carlo variation, not independent trajectories.

split.development: dataset 1, robot 1, seed 0 smoke test only; no tuning or endpoint selection
split.window: first 1200 seconds supported jointly by odometry, landmark measurements, and the timestamp support of Robot Groundtruth.dat; ground-truth values are used only for scoring, never by the filter
split.observation_subsampling: keep the first measurement timestamp at least 1.0 s after the preceding retained timestamp; retain every landmark row at that timestamp
split.map: all static landmark coordinates provided in each archive's Landmark_Groundtruth.dat are shared known-map input; the available map is archive-specific
split.odometry_interpretation: piecewise-constant logged velocity commands are treated as right-continuous at each timestamp; this is fixed before evaluation because the public page does not specify an alternative interval convention
split.raw_ingest_repair: if odometry timestamps are out of order, stable-sort odometry rows by timestamp and record the inversion count; non-odometry timestamp inversions are a hard failure
split.unresolvable_measurements: drop measurement rows whose barcode is absent from Barcodes.dat because no landmark subject/map coordinate can be assigned; record the dropped row count and do not reinterpret the barcode
split.truth: Robot Groundtruth.dat pose values are evaluator-only and are never used for initialization, map construction, filtering, or tuning; its timestamp support is used only to require complete scoring coverage

seeds.purpose: algorithmic Monte Carlo repetition on each fixed sequence

budget_contract.scalar_observation_evaluations: reported separately as state x range-bearing-pair evaluations; it is not added to the state/batch budget

primary_endpoint: radial position RMSE (m) of pre-move/post-assimilation weighted estimates at retained event timestamps

analysis.paired: Within each fixed dataset and seed, method minus B-stable
analysis.interval: percentile bootstrap over the 30 paired seeds, conditional on each sequence
analysis.multiplicity: descriptive; no claim of dataset-level generalization from two sequences
not_allowed: treating seeds as independent real trajectories
calling Q variants a complete source-QGPF reproduction

raw_data_handling: Raw third-party archives, truth arrays, and observation arrays remain in local-data outside the public repository; the repository publishes code, protocol, hashes, aggregate metrics and figures only.

amendments.change: The protocol now describes the archive-provided map rather than assuming 15 landmarks; Dataset 8 contains 14 mapped landmark subjects and one unresolved barcode is retained as a dropped-input count. The joint timestamp-support rule is stated explicitly; pose values remain evaluator-only. These are ingest clarifications made before the held-out outcome comparison, not parameter tuning.
